precepts.text: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light. That is the light Job walked by.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Job looks back on his life: “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”. When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. But what does “by his light I walked through darkness” mean?

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is the lamp, and the law is the light.

That is the light Job walked by. We can only walk through darkness the way Job did: with God’s commandments. Job kept the law, and that law was the light that carried him through a dark world.

precepts.text: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids. For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread. A lot of us are weak to the woman. The eyelashes are there for a reason; that dainty look is designed to take you. Do not let it take you over. And the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.
precepts.point: Today's traps: the thirst traps. Flee fornication. Get away from it. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body. Once you go outside of Christ, you are sinning against your own self; you put yourself in that predicament.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
Today's traps are the thirst traps. “Flee fornication”: get away from it. Solomon shows how the trap works: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.”

A lot of us are weak to the woman, weak to the box. Them eyelashes are there for a reason: batting them, fluffing them, all dainty. You noticed in the cartoons back in the day, in a little love scene, the eyelashes seem to grow. That little dainty look on the eyelids is designed to take you. Don't let it get you. Don't let it take you over.

“For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.” She is hunting, and what she hunts is your life.

That is why Paul says “he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.” Once you go outside of Christ, you are sinning against your own self. It is on you; you put yourself in that predicament. So flee it before the eyes and the heart are taken.

precepts.text: Lust not after her beauty in thine heart, neither let her take thee with her eyelids. She gives you the look back, the sparks fly, and you have lost your mind.
precepts.point: Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage. She looks good, I have to marry her so I can have her.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

precepts.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
precepts.point: Especially those who know the scriptures and choose not to obey them: that is a proud look.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

precepts.text: Jealousy is the rage of a man; he will not spare in the day of vengeance nor regard any ransom; that is why no plea could reach Potiphar.
precepts.point: When his master heard the words of his wife, his wrath was kindled and he put Joseph into the prison. He did not seek understanding, for jealousy is the rage of a man: he will not spare in the day of vengeance, nor regard any ransom.

note.label: Genesis 39: Joseph in Potiphar's House

precepts.why:
“For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance. He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.” That is why no plea could reach Potiphar. When he heard the words of his wife, “his wrath was kindled”, and he put Joseph into the prison where the king’s prisoners were bound. He did not seek understanding; jealousy is the rage of a man.

The same place shows what adultery would have cost Joseph had he done it: “whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul. A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.” Joseph refused the sin and still got the prison, because a jealous man will not spare in the day of vengeance nor regard any ransom.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; commandments and law are one and the same.
precepts.point: The Lord said, Come up to me into the mount, and I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written, that thou mayest teach them. This lets you know the law and the commandments are one and the same; Christianity tries to separate the law from the commandments, but the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, lamp and light, one and the same. These are the things you build your faith on, tearing down imaginations in the minds of our people with the word of God.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
The Lord told Moses, “I will give thee tables of stone, and a law, and commandments which I have written; that thou mayest teach them.” Law and commandments together, in one gift. Proverbs shows they are one and the same: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

Lamp and light. Christianity tries to separate the law from the commandments, but the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, one and the same. These are the things you build your faith on, tearing down imaginations in the minds of our people with the word of God.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light; that is the light that is missing in them that speak not according to the word.
precepts.point: Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 6: Teach Them Diligently unto Thy Children

precepts.why:
“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. That is the light that is missing in them that speak not according to the word.

Isaiah says if they speak not according to the law and the testimony there is no light in them; Solomon shows what that light is, the commandment and the law. A testimony that cannot come back to the commandments has no lamp. Diligently keep the commandments, the testimonies and the statutes, and you walk in the light.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light: the marvellous light we were called into.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
Peter says we were called out of darkness into his marvellous light. What is that light? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

The commandment is a lamp and the law is light: the marvellous light we were called into is the commandments and the law. We were called out of our sins into the light, and that is why the Lord avouched his peculiar people “that thou shouldest keep all his commandments”.

precepts.text: Among the six things the Lord hates, yea seven that are an abomination unto him, are hands that shed innocent blood; that is the boat Saul put himself in.
precepts.point: Saul hearkened unto Jonathan and sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain; and Jonathan brought David back to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.” That is the boat Saul put himself in when he sought to “sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause.”

For that moment Saul heard it: “Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain.” And Jonathan brought David to Saul, “and he was in his presence, as in times past.”

precepts.text: The one who commits adultery with another man's wife lacks understanding and destroys his own soul; jealousy is the rage of a man and he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
precepts.point: If his heart was deceived by a woman or he laid wait at his neighbor's door, then let his wife grind unto another and let others bow down upon her. Job is saying if he committed adultery let the same come back on him, for this is a heinous crime, a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all his increase.

note.label: Job 31: The Words Of Job Are Ended

precepts.why:
Job says, “If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door; Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.” If he committed adultery, let the same come back on him, “For this is an heinous crime; yea, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.”

Proverbs shows how heinous: “So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.” Men do not despise a thief who steals to satisfy his soul when he is hungry, and if he is found he restores sevenfold. “But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul. A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.”

“For jealousy is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance. He will not regard any ransom; neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.” The punishment of adultery is severe, and there is not much a man can do if he finds it out. That is why a lot of men die nowadays sleeping with other men's wives, and a lot of people are in jail behind one. It is a fire that consumeth to destruction and would root out all a man's increase.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
precepts.point: The light is not a mystery: it is the commandment and the law. That is what leads a man to the altar of the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 43: Send Out Thy Light and Thy Truth

precepts.why:
“O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me unto thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles.” The light is not a mystery: “the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The light is the commandment and the law.

That is what leads a man to the altar of the Most High. The commandment is the lamp and the law is the light that bring him to the holy hill and the tabernacles, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life along that road.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light; the commandments are the light.
precepts.point: Rejoice in the Lord ye righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness. He did not forget us; He chastened us for a little but He did not forget, and He is going to remember the covenant.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Light is sown for the righteous. What is the light? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandments are the light.

That light gets sown in your mind by keeping it, and gladness comes to the upright in heart with it: loving the Lord with all our heart and soul, loving our neighbour as ourself, and bringing forth fruits of repentance like God wants us to.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, so the light showed us is the laws of the Most High.
precepts.point: God is the Lord which has showed us light. The light is the laws, and we are to bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good and His mercy endures forever unto the children of the promise.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“God is the Lord, which hath shewed us light”. The light is the laws: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

The light he has shewed us is the laws of the Most High. Having that light, we bind the sacrifice with cords unto the horns of the altar and give thanks unto the Lord, for he is good, and his mercy endureth for ever unto the children of the promise.

precepts.text: The commandment is a lamp and the law is light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
precepts.point: The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life to get eternal life.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.” The lamp ordained for the anointed is Christ, the light that came into this world of darkness. And “the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is a lamp to correct us, a reproof and instruction in the way of life, to get eternal life.

precepts.text: Judah becomes surety for Benjamin, guaranteeing his safe return and willing to bear the blame forever.
precepts.point: A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger, Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth”. A surety in today's terms is like co-signing for someone, vouching that they are good and guaranteeing they will be taken care of.

Judah did exactly that for Benjamin: “And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones. I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever”. Judah becomes surety for Benjamin, guaranteeing his safe return and willing to bear the blame forever.

That is what surety is: the words of your mouth bind you for another man. Judah's word snared him to Benjamin's fate, and that is why Solomon says to go, humble yourself and make sure your friend, and deliver yourself.

precepts.text: The man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.
precepts.point: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands, and poverty comes as one that travels and want as an armed man. This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.” The ant, with no guide, overseer or ruler, provides her meat in the summer and gathers her food in the harvest; the sluggard folds his hands and poverty comes.

Paul says what that means for a man with a house: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” The man who provides not for his own house has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.

This is why in the proving stage the sisters and leadership ask a brother whether he works, has his own place, and can provide for a woman and offspring. Leadership keeps a report on these men so there are no back-door marriages. A sluggard cannot provide for his own, and a man who cannot provide has denied the faith.

precepts.text: The daughters of Zion are haughty with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, the proud look the Most High hates.
precepts.point: A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look”. He cannot be all love if he hates certain things, and the first thing on the list is a proud look.

Isaiah shows it on the daughters of Zion: “Moreover the Lord saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet”. Haughty, with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing: that is the proud look the Most High hates, and here it is on his own people's daughters.

precepts.text: The kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force; the nations have taken it by the sword.
precepts.point: A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
The Lord hates “hands that shed innocent blood”. Christ says: “And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force; the nations have taken it by the sword.

The hands that took the kingdom by force are hands that shed innocent blood. Because the Most High hates those hands, the murderers among Esau and the nations that took us captive and shed our blood have no place ruling over us in the kingdom, yet our people keep trying to get them in.

precepts.text: By the sword shalt thou live is Esau's blessing; he lives by the sword to kill and take what he wants.
precepts.point: A heart that devises wicked imaginations such as sex changes, homosexuality and lesbianism; feet swift running to mischief such as gangs and gang initiation; a false witness that speaks lies; and he that sows discord among brethren through gossip and heresies.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
The Lord hates “hands that shed innocent blood”. Esau's blessing from Isaac was: “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.”

By the sword shalt thou live is Esau's blessing; he lives by the sword to kill and take what he wants. His hands are the hands that shed innocent blood, the ones the Most High hates.

So the murderers among Esau and the nations that took us captive and shed our blood have no place ruling over us in the kingdom, yet our people keep trying to get them in. The Most High cannot be all love if he hates certain things, and he hates the hands Esau lives by.

precepts.text: Do not gaze on a maid, because looking is looking to lust.
precepts.point: A man cannot take fire in his bosom and not be burned, nor go on hot coals and not be burned; so he that goes in to his neighbour's wife and touches her shall not be innocent.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The heart is your mind, and the lust starts there, with the looking.

Ecclesiasticus says not to start: “Gaze not on a maid, that thou fall not by those things that are precious in her.” Do not gaze on a maid, because looking is looking to lust. The gaze is how she takes you with her eyelids, and the fall comes by those things that are precious in her.

By means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread, and the adulteress hunts for the precious life. It begins with the eyes, so keep them off her.

precepts.text: The adulterer thinks no one sees, but the eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun and he shall be punished where he suspected not.
precepts.point: Jealousy is the rage of a man; in the day of vengeance he will spare nothing and regard no ransom. Let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul. A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.” Ecclesiasticus lays out the adulterer's mind: “A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins”.

He thinks no one sees. “Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, and the walls do not cover anything from him. “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die.”

Then the end: “This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken.” That is the wound and dishonour. Jealousy is the rage of a man, and in the day of vengeance he spares nothing and regards no ransom: let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him. He is taken where he suspected not.
